pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Where should you look to check an answer to a comprehension question? (1 mark)
   A. In your imagination only
   B. Back at the text
   C. At the ceiling
   D. In another book only

2. Which word in this sentence is singular: The seller has an onion and two cabbages? (1 mark)
   A. seller has
   B. two
   C. onion
   D. cabbages

3. What should you do if you make a mistake in your exercise book? (1 mark)
   A. Tear the page
   B. Rub it out gently or draw one neat line through it
   C. Blame a friend
   D. Scribble over it hard

4. What is a good response when you did not understand an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Do anything
   B. Politely ask the speaker to repeat it
   C. Leave
   D. Guess quietly

5. Which sentence should be read with a rising voice in English? (1 mark)
   A. We go to school.
   B. Come to school.
   C. Are you coming to school?
   D. You are coming to school.

6. What is wrong with: it rained all night. (1 mark)
   A. It needs no changes
   B. It needs two full stops
   C. It needs a capital letter at the start
   D. It needs a comma after it

7. What does a full stop show? (1 mark)
   A. A sudden feeling
   B. The end of a statement
   C. A question
   D. A list of items

8. Which question word asks about a place? (1 mark)
   A. Who
   B. Why
   C. When
   D. Where

9. What should you do when a stranger offers you a lift? (1 mark)
   A. Go with them
   B. Accept sweets
   C. Say no politely and tell a trusted adult
   D. Give your name

10. In a written dialogue the speaker's name usually comes (1 mark)
   A. on a different page
   B. at the start of the line
   C. in the middle of a word
   D. at the end

11. Which order is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Eat, go, wash, wake up
   B. Go to school, wake up, wash, eat
   C. Wake up, wash, eat breakfast, go to school
   D. Wash, go, wake up, eat

12. What is a paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. A title
   B. One word
   C. A group of sentences about one main idea
   D. A page number

13. Where do oral narratives come from? (1 mark)
   A. From nowhere
   B. From elders and storytellers who pass them on
   C. From machines only
   D. From only one book

14. What does pronunciation mean? (1 mark)
   A. The length of a story
   B. The meaning of a word
   C. The way we write words
   D. The way we say the sounds of words

15. What is a portfolio of proverbs? (1 mark)
   A. A game
   B. A poem
   C. A folder where proverbs are collected and kept
   D. A kind of bag for money

16. Which comma use is correct? (1 mark)
   A. When the bell rang we, ran.
   B. When the bell rang, we ran.
   C. When the bell, rang we ran.
   D. When, the bell rang we ran.

17. Why might a class record narrations on a device? (1 mark)
   A. To erase them
   B. To waste time
   C. To listen back and improve
   D. To sell them

18. What is a personal experience? (1 mark)
   A. A rule
   B. A number
   C. A story from a book
   D. Something that happened to you

19. Which group of words is a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. The customer pays fifty shillings.
   B. Pays fifty
   C. Fifty shillings
   D. The customer in the market

20. Which starting sentence would make a reader curious? (1 mark)
   A. One cloudy afternoon, Neema saw a thin dog under a tree.
   B. Yes.
   C. Page one.
   D. The end.

21. Which is a constructive leisure activity? (1 mark)
   A. Fighting
   B. Reading a book
   C. Harming others
   D. Wasting money

22. Where can you find correct interjections for your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. By guessing
   B. By inventing them
   C. By copying from another language
   D. By listening to and asking elders and teachers

23. What should a dialogue about leisure show? (1 mark)
   A. Unkindness
   B. Good values such as responsibility
   C. Rudeness
   D. Bad habits

24. Which adjective describes size? (1 mark)
   A. red
   B. soft
   C. tiny
   D. round

25. Which is a common field on a form? (1 mark)
   A. Name
   B. Type of soil
   C. Colour of the wall
   D. The number of windows

26. What should you do after filling a form? (1 mark)
   A. Give it to anyone
   B. Throw it away
   C. Ignore it
   D. Check it and sign and date it

27. Which is a good quality of a leader? (1 mark)
   A. Rudeness
   B. Honesty
   C. Laziness
   D. Cruelty

28. Which is the first step in understanding a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Copy it
   C. Tear it
   D. Read the title and the poem aloud

29. Which two words in the poem Lead with honesty rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. poem and song
   B. fair and strong
   C. leader and rule
   D. all and call

30. What is a choral poem? (1 mark)
   A. A silent poem
   B. A written test
   C. A poem performed by a group together
   D. A map

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give three rules of good telephone manners. (3 marks)

32. List three ways of taking good care of a domestic animal. (3 marks)

33. Give two adjectives to describe a mobile phone. (2 marks)

34. Give two examples of constructive leisure activities. (2 marks)

35. Give three qualities of a good leader mentioned in the model poem lead with honesty. (3 marks)

36. Describe how you would play Simon says with your class and say what it teaches. (5 marks)

37. Write a short story of five sentences that ends with the proverb A stitch in time saves nine. (5 marks)

38. Read: Mama Wanjiru buys tomatoes, an onion and three cabbages at the market. List the nouns and say which are singular and which are plural. (5 marks)

39. Give three money words and their meanings. (3 marks)

40. Pick out the nouns in this song line: We roast the maize and boil the beans. (3 marks)

41. List the two verbs in the sentence: The teacher counted the votes and announced the winner. (2 marks)

42. What is a verb? Give two examples. (2 marks)

43. Give two rules for filling in a form correctly. (2 marks)

44. Name three headings in a story plan. (3 marks)

45. List three tips for reciting a poem well. (3 marks)

46. Describe how to read a passage with interjections aloud. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — MOCK EXAM #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Back at the text
   Good readers go back to the text.

2. C — onion
   Onion names one thing. Cabbages is plural.

3. B — Rub it out gently or draw one neat line through it
   Neat correction keeps the page clean.

4. B — Politely ask the speaker to repeat it
   Polite questions help you understand.

5. C — Are you coming to school?
   It is a question.

6. C — It needs a capital letter at the start
   The first word of a sentence must begin with a capital letter.

7. B — The end of a statement
   A full stop ends a statement.

8. D — Where
   Where asks for the place.

9. C — Say no politely and tell a trusted adult
   Personal safety means not going with strangers.

10. B — at the start of the line
   The name shows who speaks.

11. C — Wake up, wash, eat breakfast, go to school
   This is the natural order of a morning routine.

12. C — A group of sentences about one main idea
   A paragraph has one main idea.

13. B — From elders and storytellers who pass them on
   They are passed on by word of mouth.

14. D — The way we say the sounds of words
   Pronunciation is how words are said.

15. C — A folder where proverbs are collected and kept
   A portfolio holds the class collection.

16. B — When the bell rang, we ran.
   A comma follows the when part at the start.

17. C — To listen back and improve
   Recordings show what to improve.

18. D — Something that happened to you
   A personal experience is an event you lived.

19. A — The customer pays fifty shillings.
   It has a subject and a predicate.

20. A — One cloudy afternoon, Neema saw a thin dog under a tree.
   A specific opening makes the reader want to read on.

21. B — Reading a book
   Constructive activities build people up.

22. D — By listening to and asking elders and teachers
   Speakers know the correct forms.

23. B — Good values such as responsibility
   Dialogues can teach values.

24. C — tiny
   Tiny describes size.

25. A — Name
   Name is a common field.

26. D — Check it and sign and date it
   Checking prevents mistakes.

27. B — Honesty
   Good leaders are honest and fair.

28. D — Read the title and the poem aloud
   Reading aloud comes first.

29. D — all and call
   All and call have the same ending sound.

30. C — A poem performed by a group together
   Chorus means together.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greet, give your name, speak clearly, do not interrupt, do not call late without a reason, say goodbye.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give food and clean water, provide a shelter, take it to a veterinary doctor when sick, do not overload it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: small, black, thin, new, flat (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sensible adjective.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Reading, sports, drawing, singing, gardening, community service (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fair, true, listens, shares the work, kind, strong (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: One pupil is the leader. The leader gives instructions. Pupils obey only when the leader says Simon says. Those who obey a wrong instruction are out. The game teaches careful listening.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the leader, one for the rule, one for what happens when a player breaks the rule, and two marks for explaining what it teaches.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five clear sentences with a beginning, problem, ending and the proverb used correctly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence up to four and one mark for using the proverb correctly.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: Nouns: Mama Wanjiru, tomatoes, onion, cabbages, market. Singular: Mama Wanjiru, onion, market. Plural: tomatoes, cabbages.
   Working / marking points: One mark for finding all five nouns, two marks for correct singular nouns and two marks for correct plural nouns.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Trade: buying and selling. Profit: money gained. Customer: person who buys. Price: cost of something.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each word with its meaning.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: maize and beans (and we is a pronoun, not a noun)
   Working / marking points: One mark for maize, one mark for beans, and one mark for not including roast or boil, which are actions.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: counted, announced
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb. Teacher, votes and winner are nouns.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: A verb is an action word. Examples: run, close, bring, put.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one mark for two correct examples.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Read instructions first, write neatly inside the spaces, give true information, sign and date it (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each heading.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Learn it well, mark pauses and stressed words, speak clearly, look at the audience, keep a steady pace.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each tip.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, find the interjections, decide the feeling of each, read each with the right voice, and keep a steady pace.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.
